_note: Reference/documentation copy of the character portion of new_campaign_state.json (the file engine.py actually loads for a fresh game). Keep these in sync if you tune starting values.
name: Alfred, King of the West Saxons

attribute_notes.oration: A capable speaker but not a natural crowd-charmer - his power comes more from what he says than how he says it.
attribute_notes.intellect: His defining trait - the scholar-king reputation is earned even this early, before the famous translation projects of the 880s-890s.
attribute_notes.resolve: Extraordinary endurance under sustained crisis - this is the attribute the Athelney arc is built to test.
attribute_notes.presence: Competent at court but not magnetic - see the untrained wooing_and_alliance skill.
attribute_notes.cunning: Genuinely underrated by his enemies, which is itself an asset - see the Edington campaign's use of misdirection historically.
attribute_notes.physique: Deliberately his weakest attribute, reflecting a real, recurring illness attested by his biographer Asser - see the Chronic Affliction liability.

untrained_of_note: tongues_of_the_realm (no Norse yet - a plausible growth arc)

note_on_growth: Starts as a king already under siege, not a blank slate - his growth arc over the campaign is less 'become powerful' and more 'survive, then rebuild Wessex, then unify the English response to the Danes,' tracked mostly through the saxon_unity and military_readiness resources and the contingent canon events (Athelney, Edington, Wedmore) rather than raw levels.
